entries.title: ship the standard library with the native compiler
entries.body:
Every native release from 0.1.1 to 0.4.0 staged `bin`, `runtime` and `scripts`
into the tarball and no `std/`, so the compiler they carry links `hello.ts` and
answers any program importing the standard library by its package specifier
with ``Module `nish/text` is not part of the standard library``. The sentence
names the module it refuses, because stage1's list is a literal and the file is
what is absent. Both channels are fixed, and nothing had been published to npm,
so it lands before the first publish.

It was found by `nish-cmp`, which this also wires into CI as a job sharing the
`seeds` job with `bootstrap` -- WP19 §5a's "single biggest unstarted piece of
R6". `cmpSince` in `.github/seed-targets.json` decides which releases it may
compare against, for the reason `attachedSince` exists: a release already
published cannot grow a file.

Also: `packageRoot()` resolves a bare `argv[0]` through `$PATH`, so unpacking a
release tarball onto `$PATH` is an install again; the release bump moves the
lockfile's platform pins, which it had been reading from the wrong place since
the installer landed; and §5a records measurements for items 5 and 6 and says
which release R6 can land in, which is not 0.5.0 -- `nish-cmp` has no row until
0.5.0 is out, so deleting the two largest oracles in it would do so during the
one window their successor cannot run.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: realpathSync, the path resolution a symlinked install needs
entries.body:
`packageRoot()` resolves no symbolic link, so a compiler reached through one
looks for `scripts/build.sh` and `std/` beside the LINK rather than beside the
package. npm links every command that way, and so does an admin's
`ln -s /opt/nish/bin/nish /usr/local/bin/nish` -- measured, that second one
fails `--link` in both spellings, by the link's absolute path as well as by the
bare name, because a link IS a path and the `$PATH` lookup cannot reach it.

`realpathSync(path: string): string | null` is `getenv`'s shape exactly: one
call, an `i8*` that may be null, read by the ordinary `T | null` narrowing. In
both compilers, the runtime and the Node shim, so the oracles compare them.

`self/`'s own `packageRoot()` still cannot call it: `self/` compiles under the
last RELEASED compiler and no release has the builtin, which CI's `bootstrap`
job checks. The call site is the next release's; the freeze was verified green
on all four platforms with the builtin added and unused.

`realpath(p, NULL)` is the shorter spelling and the wrong one -- on Darwin the
`__DARWIN_EXTSN` variant implements it and the binding depends on the
feature-macro level, while a caller-supplied PATH_MAX buffer is defined under
both. The declaration needs `_XOPEN_SOURCE 700`: `realpath` is XSI, and on
glibc 2.39 the POSIX macro alone leaves it undeclared, with clang then
inferring `int`.
metrics: nish_realpath is 157 bytes of .text at -Oz; the portable spelling costs 8 of them. The runtime_os.c ceiling moves 1,280 -> 1,536, the move wp7 said the next OS-facing builtin would make.
tests: and a tests/run.js check resolving a real file symlink and a directory symlink
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon
